# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 70 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 70 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_070_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 70 opens Similitude 8 — a new and elaborate vision distinct from the Similitude 6-7 material that preceded it. The willow tree (*itea*) is the central image. All who have been called by the name of the Lord shelter under it. An angel distributes rods cut from the willow, and the varying states of the rods — green, dry, cracked, half-and-half, with or without shoots — encode the spiritual states of the recipients.

This is a classic Hermas allegory structured for systematic unpacking: the vision comes first, then the interpretation chapter by chapter. The willow tree itself remains unharmed by the cutting, which the shepherd explains: pruning does not damage a healthy tree.

The angel is described as *endoxos kai hypsēlos* — "glorious and tall/high." EMET has "glorious and very tall," LOGOS the same, PNEUMA "towering and magnificent." SOPHIA adopts "glorious and very tall" as the more literal rendering.

The rods (*rhabdous*) are distributed at roughly a cubit (*pēchys*, forearm length). EMET/LOGOS preserve "cubit," PNEUMA renders "forearm's length." SOPHIA uses "cubit" as it is both accurate and familiar enough in English.

The enumeration of rod types in 70:5 is a challenge for all agents — it must be systematic and clear. All three agents handle this similarly; SOPHIA follows LOGOS's ordering most closely.

---

## Similitude 8, Part 1 — The Great Willow Tree

**70:1** He showed me a great willow tree overshadowing fields and mountains, and all those who had been called by the name of the Lord had come and gathered under the shadow of the willow.

**70:2** And there stood an angel of the Lord, glorious and very tall, with a great sickle, and he was cutting branches from the willow and distributing them to the people sheltered under the tree. He gave to each of them small rods, about a cubit in length.

**70:3** After all had received rods, the angel set aside his sickle, and the tree appeared healthy, just as I had seen it before.

**70:4** I marveled at this within myself and said: "How can this tree be healthy after having so many branches cut from it?" The shepherd said to me: "Do not marvel. The tree will remain healthy after all its branches have been pruned."

**70:5** "But why did some receive green branches and others dry ones? Why were some completely withered and dry, others cracked, others green but dried at the tips, others half-green and half-dry, others more dry than green, others more green than dry, and still others had shoots growing from them — some with healthy tips, others with dried tips?"

**70:6** "Explain to me, lord," I said, "what the various kinds of rods mean — for I am troubled by all of this." He answered me: "Listen and I will explain to you the meaning of every rod."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
